name: LIGO — dark matter searches
full_name: Laser Interferometer Gravitational-Wave Observatory dark-matter searches
summary: A two-site US gravitational-wave observatory also directly testing ultralight scalar, vector and tensor dark matter through mirror and beam-splitter responses, and conducting astronomical searches including primordial black holes.
detection_principle: Ultralight fields can change optical-component dimensions, exert baryon-dependent forces or produce strainlike tensor responses; the two interferometers are analyzed spectrally and cross-correlated.

status.label: Published experimental record; current overall operating status unverified
status.evidence: 2026 sources support the phase recorded here, rather than a real-time status of the entire project as of the access date.

key_parameters.name: Interferometer arm length
key_parameters.value: Hanford and Livingston each have two 4 km arms.

phases.name: Advanced LIGO O3
phases.description: Used jointly with Virgo data for dark-photon searches.

phases.name: Advanced LIGO O4a
phases.description: H1/L1 provide the scalar, vector and tensor direct-dark-matter searches; the analysis does not use data from all three LVK observatories.

results.summary: The O4a three-model search published in 2026 found no dark-matter evidence and set model-specific coupling limits. Although authored by LVK, it actually used the two LIGO detectors' data.

science_scope: A multipurpose gravitational-wave observatory covering direct ultralight-field searches and astronomical dark-matter candidates. Ordinary gravitational-wave detection is not a dark-matter discovery; primordial-black-hole interpretations require separate tests.
